prompt.en: How can a country's economic choices today shape its future? Why should it think about future results when it decides today? (3 marks)

label.en: Explains that today's allocation of scarce resources commits land, labour and capital for years — building capacity or locking in losses

level1.en: A factory or a forest takes years, not days. So what does choosing between them today do to tomorrow's options?

clue.en: Whatever a country builds, grows or extracts now fixes what its people can produce — and what they will lack — for decades.

level2Template.en: Present choices shape the future because the resources committed today determine the country's ___ for years to come.

label.en: Gives a concrete example such as investing in education/health versus quick-profit crops, or conserving soil/water versus exhausting them

level1.en: Recall sugarcane versus millets: one pays now, the other keeps paying for many years. Which choice still matters years later?

clue.en: Money put into schools and hospitals returns as skilled, healthy workers; water mined today returns as empty wells tomorrow.

level2Template.en: For example, expenditure on ___ builds future capacity, whereas the exhaustion of resources today creates shortages tomorrow.

label.en: Argues why future consequences must be weighed — some costs last for many years and many choices are hard to undo

level1.en: If a bad choice could be undone next year, thinking ahead would hardly matter. Why can countries not simply undo theirs?

clue.en: A cut forest, used-up underground water, children who missed school — some costs cannot be undone later.

level2Template.en: Future results must be weighed because many decisions, once taken, are ___.

text.en: Economic choices made today shape the economy for many years, so their future results need careful thought.
Present choices shape the future because the resources committed today determine the country's ___ for years to come.
For example, expenditure on ___ builds future capacity, whereas the exhaustion of resources today creates shortages tomorrow.
Future results must be weighed because many decisions, once taken, are ___.
